The remembered moments of the first weeks and the squad's paragraph; written by the mechanic model, or from templates.
The longest text one remembered fact keeps, in characters. A longer text is cut; the setting is yours and survives a change of preset.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A fact is one short line the squad remembers. A higher number keeps more of what a model wrote (the first weeks, a scene summary, your own edits) and takes more of the memory share of the prompt; a lower one keeps lines terse. It applies to facts written from now on and to every edit. The short template facts of character development keep their own shorter cap.

short: Soldiers change slowly from what they live through. Nothing announces it: it shows in how she acts, and her file records it afterwards.
long: What she lives through and what she sees done around her is weighed from her side: was it wanted, who began it, how it ended. Small amounts add up, and now and then a review turns them into a nudge or a step of a value, a taste or a bond field. Her card never changes, and her own limits never move.

short: A step that has already shown in how she acts, written into her file after the scene where it showed.
long: Nothing is announced when it happens: the next scene she is in carries a quiet cue, and the line appears here afterwards.

short: A line about who she has become, in words: an attitude, a habit, a skill, a memory.
long: Reviews and habits write them. The main model reads them as who she is now. With the edit lock off they can be edited or removed.

short: Something she has done often enough to be hers: a drill she keeps, a person she keeps near, ground she knows.
long: Most habits are only words in her file. A few carry a small effect on the activity they come from.

short: Freezes one line of her development: it keeps what it has and takes no more pushes or steps.
long: Only with the edit lock off.

short: How she read an event: was it wanted, who began it, whether it caused harm, how it ended.
long: She may be wrong about what she only saw from the side. When the truth reaches her, her reading is revised. Which events she misread is never shown.

short: The mechanic model words each habit a soldier forms in one call; off, the registry's text stands.
How she talks and carries herself: how much she speaks, whether she is steady or moody, and what kind of humor she has.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Three words describe her temperament. They shape how often she shares what happens to her, how she takes a hard word and whether she makes a joke. They are set at import and can be changed, and a locked one stays as it is.

short: How readily she speaks: silent, terse or talkative.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A talkative soldier tells you her news and brings things up on her own. A silent one keeps most of it to herself and has to be asked.

short: Steady or moody. A moody soldier takes a hard word harder, and her mood shows.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A steady soldier takes a blow and carries on. A moody one is shaken by it and holds it longer.

short: What kind of jokes she makes: none, dry, mocking or warm.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Humor decides whether she brings back a running joke and in what spirit. None means she never does.

short: What happens to her when you are not there: a broken mug, a letter, a bad night. Most stay hers; some she tells you.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A day off-screen can bring something small or something that matters. What she keeps to herself is never shown. What she tells you arrives in its own time, as a message, a word when you next meet, or a line on the hub.

short: What she has to tell you waits its turn, so that you hear one thing at a time.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Her news comes at a pace: no more than a few items a day across the squad, never the same kind twice in a row. Old news becomes a passing mention. Which item comes next is never shown.

short: A hobby is picked up, practiced, stalls, cools, is put away and sometimes taken up again.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: She practices where she spends her slots. Progress comes in steps, each with its own moment. Interest rises and falls, and a hobby she drops can return. How far she has come is shown by what she says and what she keeps, never as a number.

short: A meeting with no stakes: cooking, the roof in the rain, cards. Both of you are at ease, and it brings you closer.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A quiet meeting takes a slot and opens a scene that is only what it is. It lowers her stress and warms her a little, and the first time something happens in one, it is remembered.

short: What she thinks about things, in her own words. A view appears once she has told you.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Opinions form when something brings a subject up. She voices one once, when it fits. A view she holds firmly changes only slowly, and only if you argue it well.

short: Something you and she keep coming back to. After a few returns it is yours.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A joke she has shared with you can come back. Three returns within a month make it a running joke. Whether she brings one up depends on her humor.

short: How far you have learned a hobby from her: none, a beginner, getting there, good at it.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Spending time on her hobby teaches you a little, and a soldier who is good at it and likes to teach, teaches faster. It is only a description: it changes nothing else.

short: How often things happen to her off-screen: off, rare, normal or often. Off keeps the days as they were.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Off, nothing happens to her when you are not there. A running campaign can switch it on at any time; what already happened stays.

short: Whether she may ever come to hold authority over the commander: yes, no, or auto (it follows her profile).
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: No keeps her out of the dynamic whatever her profile says. Yes lets her in if her profile allows it. Auto lets her profile decide. This is a switch of the campaign, not hers.

short: How fast she takes to the dynamic: sluggish, normal or lively. It scales how much each probe moves her.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A sluggish soldier takes half of what a probe would give; a lively one takes it and more. It changes the pace for her alone, not what she wants.

short: She starts with a head start in the dynamic: her hold begins a little above zero.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A seed is checked against her profile when the campaign starts. A seeded soldier does not need an inclination, and she can start already in a frame. At most as many seeds as holders.

short: The frame a seeded soldier begins in: none (equal), play or role. The hold of that frame comes with it.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Equal is the default: nothing is settled. Play and role begin the campaign after the first steps were already taken. No milestone is played for it.

short: With a head start, the dynamic has had its first probes behind the scenes: she has already been tested.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Only with a head start above zero. The answers are decided by the setup alone, hold stays inside the testing band, and a moment or two may be remembered. Without this option the head start leaves the dynamic at zero.

short: The dynamic's hold, frame and readings are shown as feelings and words, never as values.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Only what is displayed changes. The engine counts exactly as before.

short: Who words what a holder asks of the commander: the mechanic model, from a few examples, or a plain line with no model call.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: With the model, every task, punishment or hold is worded in her own voice; the engine still decides what it weighs and what it costs. With plain lines nothing is sent to a model and the wording is the example's own. Either way only the words differ.

short: How many soldiers may hold authority over the commander at once: none, one, two, three or any number.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: None switches the dynamic off. Lowering the number later ends nothing: a holder keeps her place, and only new probes, offers and milestones are held back.

short: How fast hold moves: slow, normal or fast.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Pace scales every gain and loss of hold. It does not change what she wants or which frames exist.

short: How often something comes of it: rare, normal or often. It scales the daily chance of a probe or a claim.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Only the chance moves; what a probe is, and what it can give, does not.

short: How often a moment of tension comes up in a scene while something is live: rare, normal or often.
long: A moment is a point where the commander gets an explicit choice. It comes only while the scene has something live (a visitor, a posture, her mood) and never twice in a row: rare, normal and often set the chance and the gap between two.

short: How often moments come up when a scene is at explicit intimacy: rarer, as often, or none.
long: At explicit intimacy the chance of a moment is halved by default, so moments do not interrupt. Same keeps the normal chance; off stops them there.

short: Show a moment as three chips, or hide the chips and answer in your own words.
long: In immersive mode the card is replaced by one dim line. What you type is read as an answer the same way.

short: A held contact runs in real time. Off: each message uses up a number of beats.
long: In real time the gauge moves on the clock and tapping out is holding a key; the stop word always works. Turn-based is the default.

short: Switch each kind of interaction of a held contact on or off. Off: only text and moment options remain.
long: Timing, hold, decision, order, passive, gesture and the breath can each be switched off.

short: How long a marathon takes in play: short, normal or long.
long: It sets how many phases a marathon has and how quickly the hours pass in the fiction.

short: The three ways to answer a moment, shown as buttons under the chat. Each can be examined; typing your own answer works too.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: When a moment comes up the card lists its answers. The words are the story's own once they arrive; until then plain words stand in. Some scenes add a fourth: asking her to lock the door, asking her with a look, or looking at a friend. The game reads what you choose, and what she makes of it is for the story to show. In immersive mode only a dim line remains and your own words are read instead.

short: After a blackout the scene is cut, time moves on and the commander comes to somewhere else. Dizzy until the day ends.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A blackout only happens with breath play switched on and a holder who goes on to the end. The scene ends, one more slot is spent, every check is one lower until the day ends, and the card tells where the commander came to.

short: A signal inside the story. What she does with it depends on how she holds: she lets go, ignores the first, or ignores them all.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The tap is a move the commander makes in the fiction. A holder who lets go at a signal stops at once; one who holds to a limit ignores the first; one who goes to blackout ignores every tap. The stop word is different: it always works.

short: Your own signal, outside the story. It always ends the hold and takes away the contact or item, whatever she holds to.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The stop word is never part of the fiction and never refused. It ends the hold at once, mid-segment or between segments, in either mode, and she stops what she is doing for the next reply.

short: What the body does in a hold and what you can do about it: one button per move, the tap, and the stop word that always works.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Turn-based, each press is one beat and the segment ends when its beats are used up. In real time, a press lands on the beat the clock is at and Space is the main input. A cue line tells what she does before the beat comes; the screen narrows and shakes as the limit nears (a static tint when motion is reduced). Typing uses up beats, and the game never waits for the model.

short: A drill at base that raises how long the commander can last in one kind of hold: breath, weight or jaw. Once a day for each.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Endurance grows by holds endured, by catching her gaps in a row, and by drilling at base. It raises the capacity of the body for that hold and never widens her gaps or changes her rhythm. The file shows it as a word, never as a number.

short: A hold of an hour of story time or more. It runs in phases, the clock shows the story time, and the slots it spans are spent.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A long hold is played in phases of a few segments. Between two phases the story time passes and you choose how to spend it. Each phase starts a little weaker than the last. When it is over the scene ends, every slot it spanned is spent and the commander is stiff until the next one. The pace setting changes only how long it takes to play, never what happens in the story.

short: Between two phases: endure it, spare strength for the next, ease the body in secret, or ask for a rest. The game decides how it went.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Endure holds with a chance that grows with the commander's endurance. Sparing strength helps the next stretch. Easing the body in secret restores something and may be caught, the way relief inputs are. Asking for a rest is granted or refused by how she holds.

short: What a contact with a mouth offers: a kiss, counted kisses, a long kiss, licking, as a pet, or taking in the mouth. Each tastes what it touches.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A kiss is one act and she reacts to it. Counted kisses are a ritual with a number she sets. A long kiss is held still. Licking works the dirt away and dries the mouth. As a pet is a quick rhythm. Taking in the mouth works the jaw. Each act is a taste of what the contact carries, and tasting grows familiar with time.

short: She sets a number. You count the kisses yourself and type the number you reached; a wrong count starts again.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The count is yours to keep: the game only checks the number you give. The same number stays until it is right.

short: What a soldier does herself as the one who leads, how she feels seeing it done and the style she leads in; read from her card.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: What a soldier does herself as the one who leads, how she feels seeing it done and the style she leads in; read from her card.

short: For each practice that is switched on: whether she would do it herself as the one who leads (craves it, enjoys it, tolerates it or not at all).
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: For each practice that is switched on: whether she would do it herself as the one who leads (craves it, enjoys it, tolerates it or not at all).

short: For each practice that is switched on: how she feels seeing it done by anyone (drawn, indifferent or disliking). Independent of whether she would do it herself.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: For each practice that is switched on: how she feels seeing it done by anyone (drawn, indifferent or disliking). Independent of whether she would do it herself.

short: How she leads: a main style and, optionally, a second one that comes through in some moments. The style sets her tone and what she does next.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: How she leads: a main style and, optionally, a second one that comes through in some moments. The style sets her tone and what she does next.

short: Who she would let see a dynamic: nobody, a few chosen friends, anyone, or she does not mind either way.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Who she would let see a dynamic: nobody, a few chosen friends, anyone, or she does not mind either way.

short: How readily she would take the lead in a dynamic of authority: not at all, only with a strong cause, with curiosity, or eagerly.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: How readily she would take the lead in a dynamic of authority: not at all, only with a strong cause, with curiosity, or eagerly.

short: How fair she is when she holds authority: fair, strict, capricious or unfair. It is independent of her style.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: How fair she is when she holds authority: fair, strict, capricious or unfair. It is independent of her style.

short: How she invites: she says it, she hints, or she expects to be understood without a word.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: How she invites: she says it, she hints, or she expects to be understood without a word.

short: How fast her desire grows, as a trait of the character and not of her style: low, moderate or high.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: How fast her desire grows, as a trait of the character and not of her style: low, moderate or high.

short: What she expects of the commander and would like to see. Hidden in play: it becomes known only as it shows.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: What she expects of the commander and would like to see. Hidden in play: it becomes known only as it shows.

short: Something she asks that would change what is between her and the commander: a first yes, a rule to keep, a handover. Accept it or refuse it, here or in words.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Accepting moves the dynamic on a step and costs nothing. Refusing is not leaving: it costs her a measure of the hold she has, and she may ask again after a week.

short: The status said aloud and kept. After it, leaving is a break, not an ending.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Once sworn, every way out of the dynamic is a break, and what follows is heavier. The vow is remembered and never fades.

short: How serious it is between them: equal, play, role or rule. It moves only through a step she asks, or when the weight goes out of it.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A number alone never moves a frame. Play is a game they play in scenes; role is a role held all day; rule is her word standing over what she has claimed.

short: A part of the commander's life she has asked for and been given: her time, the device, the command. The card lists what it lets her do.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A domain is lost when the hold behind it falls below its band, when she leaves, or to another holder who wants the same one. What each lets her do is read from what it grants, never from its name.

short: She asks for a domain, or, at the top, for the commander to give way. Yield, refuse, or talk it over: a compromise gives it to her for a week.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Refusing costs what the frame says and she waits a week before asking again. A claim asked before another holder's own is settled between the two of them.

short: What she does once the commander has left what she held: grieves, pursues, turns cold, offers to take the commander back. It runs its course or is answered.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: An aftermath is picked by her manner, her values, how far it had gone and how she was left, and runs in stages. A return offer waits for an answer: accepting begins again at a lower step, refusing ends it and is remembered.

short: Her bookings are not held to the weekly limit.
She may book the commander's evenings up to three days ahead.
She may set standing conditions on the commander's body and appearance.
She has the full run of the commander's device, whatever the usual access would be.
She may block or cancel the commander's requests to the Leash.
Service and protocol hold outside scenes, in her quarters.
Her quarters are a second home: an evening she books is spent there.
She may set rules on whom else the commander sees.
Another holder's booking of the commander's time waits for her consent.
She may overrule the commander's orders; the commander can comply, argue or defy.
The squad starts to address her as the one in command.
She holds the command and has overruled an order. Comply and her way runs; argue it out in a scene with her; or defy her and the order runs at a price.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Comply raises the hold she has and her favor. Defying costs hold and favor, counts toward the contest of authority and shows the squad who gave way. Arguing opens a scene with her alone: only a real compromise settles it.

short: File the request from the terminal in the comms room, around her hold. It costs the slot, and she may find out.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The terminal in the comms room is not on her device. Using it costs a slot and, if she finds out, counts as a defiance toward her.

short: A soldier who knows the device resets it so the request goes out unheld. The least likely to be found; it needs someone technically able.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Needs a soldier whose role or defect gives the know-how. If she finds out, it counts as a defiance toward her.

short: Another soldier files it through her own channel. The most likely to be found, and the soldier pays for it.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Only a soldier who trusts the commander will do it. If she finds out, it counts as a defiance toward her and the soldier loses trust.

short: Offer her one or two things: a part, a posture, a contact, a service, time, a role, endurance. What she craves lands; what she dislikes is a blunder.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: An offer cannot be taken back, and she may make a claim of what was offered. Asking for something in return changes how she reads the offer, not how she answers it. Offered before others, it is seen.

short: How she took the offer: accepted, corrected (she says what she wants instead, and the zone is shown), mocked, refused, or tonight.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The game decides her answer from her profile and her manner; the scene only gives it words. A correction shows the commander something of her that was not known before.

short: What the commander has been shown of how she responds, by zone. A gray ? is not known yet; a color, a word and a note come once she has shown it.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The map fills from her corrections and reactions, and from the commander's mastery of each zone: practice shows it. Dots are mastery, rings are the scent she has now, and a diamond marks a zone that needs explicit content to be on. Readable mode shows the list alone.

short: A soldier who, over time, comes to hold authority over the commander: how far it has gone, what she holds, and how it ends.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: It begins with small things she tries and the commander allows. It grows through hold, frames and the domains she claims, and it can end: abruptly, by talking it through, by handing it to another, or by force. Every number behind it belongs to the engine; the screens show words and bands.

short: How much weight her word carries with the commander. Shown as a band: interest, testing, keeping, owning, possessing.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Hold grows from what the commander lets her do and what the commander gives her, and it falls when it is left unfed. It cannot pass the testing band without a step she asks and the commander accepts. The number is shown only with show raw values, and never in immersive mode.

short: What she takes the commander to be, in her own word. It is hers, and it can be wrong.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: She forms it from how the commander answers what she tries. It tells what she believes, never what the commander feels. The word is shown only once she has read something.

short: Leaving what she holds. Always possible; what it costs is shown as a word for each route.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Abruptly costs what it costs. Talking it through opens a scene and, if a compromise is reached, makes it lighter. A transfer hands the commander to another holder. Forcing it needs a punishment, the Leash or an oversight request done first, and costs more. A vow is a break whatever the route.

short: A holder who answers for the Leash may hold the commander's requests: they go no further unless she signs. A request held spends nothing.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Every request filed from the device goes to her first, for anyone it names. She signs more readily the more she owes the commander. A held request is noted by oversight; enough of them draw its attention. The commander can go around her, and she may find out.

short: Oversight has noticed how many of the commander's Leash requests were held or never filed, and may act on the soldier who held the requests.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: It builds slowly, in notices, and the corporation's voice says each step. When it is full oversight acts on her: a reprimand, a threat to move her, or the controller used on her. Her cover slows it.

short: Something of the commander's that a holder keeps to herself. It is shown only once she has mentioned it.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: She may have seen it, or been told, or found it. Until she speaks of it nothing says it exists. Once she has, it is hers to use: in a demand, in a threat, or in telling the squad.

short: How she thinks of the commander. It is hers alone, never shown as a number or a band; it shows in how she speaks and in the squad's nicknames.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: It rises with what the commander bears with dignity and falls with what is lost before others. It does not tell what the commander feels, and no screen reads it out.

short: A small thing she tries, deniably, to see how the commander answers. The answer shapes how she reads the commander.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A probe is never an order and she can always say it was nothing. Yielding, deflecting, resisting and returning it each tell her something different. It lasts one scene.

short: How well the commander has learned to serve her in one part of the body, from none to five. Practice raises it; the xp behind it is not shown.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Mastery opens a zone on the body map once it is high enough: practice shows what she could not be asked. It is the commander's, with her, per part.

short: With the dynamic's numbers hidden you feel it rather than read it: no band, no value, no frame name. The engine counts as before.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Immersive mode changes only what is displayed. Her cards, her notices and the line on the hub still show.

short: What a holder asks of the commander: a task, a punishment, a rule, a denial or a hold. Her words are hers; what it weighs is the engine's.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A holder asks for a practice only while she holds at play or beyond. Each one has stakes: the more it weighs, the more your answer must say. What she may ask depends on what is switched on and on what she would never do.

short: Something a holder asks the commander to do, with a way to check it and often a time. Her words are hers; what it weighs and how it is judged is not.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A task is offered as a card. The commander accepts it, refuses it or talks it over. A kept task makes her hold firmer; a broken one costs her trust and may be answered.

short: A task she has put to the commander, as a card: her words, what saying yes would cost, and the answers: accept, refuse, talk.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The card shows what the task costs before the commander answers. A task the commander does not answer may run out.

short: The more a task weighs, the more saying yes asks: a button, a button that shows its cost first, words, then words and a signature.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Refusing is always one press. Saying yes to something heavy is never an accident.

short: A task this heavy is accepted by saying so, in the scene or in her thread. The button only takes the commander to the place to type.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The game reads what the commander says. Nothing is accepted by a button here, and a question is not a yes.

short: The heaviest tasks need the commander's words and then a signature, held down. The signature is kept on the record.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The line under the task says what the signature closes or hands over. Let go early and nothing is signed.

short: What the commander has signed, newest first, with the day. A sealed task is signed blank.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The record is kept by whoever asked. It is part of what she remembers.

short: She hands over an envelope. What is in it is read when the commander accepts. Refusing an envelope counts as refusing something heavy.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Some women show the weight of what is inside, some only the envelope. A sealed task is signed blank.

short: What she does when something she asked for was broken or she was refused: a card with her words, its name and its weight in a word (light, heavy, harsh).
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The weight is hers to set by what was broken, by her manner and by how often it has happened. The commander answers it: accept, negotiate or refuse.

short: Accept: it is carried out, part of the cost comes back. Negotiate: a talk may lighten it. Refuse: a defiance. UNDO takes an answer back until something follows.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: An answer cannot be taken back once the day, the slot or the scene has moved on, or once others saw it, or after anything it started has gone further.

short: She wants a soldier punished through the commander. Do it, take it instead (the soldier is spared, the commander takes the same weight), or refuse her.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The squad sees who took what. A soldier who was spared remembers it.

short: She wants to show her hold before others. Go opens the scene with those named and takes the slot; refuse is a refusal. Those who watch know of it afterwards.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Only some women stage one, and who is asked follows her own manner and the squad: the few she trusts, or whoever is at the table. Each onlooker reacts by her own stance toward what the holder leads in. Only a humbling one is seen outside the squad.

short: A posture she has named in her own words, for the ones the commander takes in her scenes. The set grows with her service.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A woman who keeps a ritual or runs the household names a posture the first time it is set in a scene with her. How many she keeps follows how far her service has gone. She may later call one by its name.

short: She calls a posture by her name for it. The right one in time counts as service; a wrong or late one is a slip. No timer if the order interaction is off.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The call comes now and then in a scene with her, once she holds more than a little. Her style sets how long the commander has.

short: A holder keeps the commander in her quarters for a slot or more. Nothing that leaves is allowed. Ask to be let go, or let the slot pass.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The hold is a booking of the commander's own slots. Other bookings in those slots lapse (another holder's is left to be settled). Scenes with her in her quarters, DMs and ending the slot go on. A duty that comes meanwhile is an alarm. A hold that runs to its end with no defiance raises her restraint and her hold.

short: The commander's sight is taken, by a hold in the dark or a blindfold: the device dims, no portraits, no header, low sound, only plain lines of text.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: It is read from the hold and from what the commander wears in the scene, never from the system's own display settings. It ends with the hold or when the blindfold comes off.

short: A plea to the holder to end the hold. Her answer follows her style and frame: she lets go, refuses in silence or in words, or keeps the commander longer.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A gentle holder lets go when she is content; a ritual one only at the end she named; a cruel one may take the plea as a reason to keep longer. The answer is the engine's and is the same every time for the same state.

short: A duty that comes while the commander is held: a launch, a mission due today, a knock at night. The holder lets go, lets go late, or keeps.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: She decides from her values, her style and her frame. A keep can be accepted, argued once or defied; defying it ends the hold and counts against the commander as an offense of hers. A keep over a launch lets the squad leave without the commander.

short: The squad left without the commander: no command points, no orders and no compel in a fight, no one exposed, and the squad decides the event nodes.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: It is only possible while a holder keeps the commander and her answer to the duty was keep. The report and the recap say so.

short: At an event node of a run without the commander the squad takes the first option that asks nothing of the commander. ACKNOWLEDGE closes the node.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Options that need the commander's own stats or a way chosen by the commander are closed to the squad. When nothing is left the node holds nothing.

short: The commander asks her for something to do. She says yes (a task is written and her hold rises), mocks the request, or turns it down. Once a day for each woman.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Her answer follows her manner, how far her hold has come and how she stands with the commander. A woman who could hold but does not yet may be asked: a yes can start it. A mocked request is seen by those in the room.

short: The commander asks her for a punishment. She gives a light one, mocks the request, or turns it down. Once a day for each woman.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: What she gives is picked by the engine from her limits and what is switched on; her manner decides whether she says yes at all. Asking another woman while a holder has the commander is for the holder to allow.

short: The commander tells her the daily routine was not done today. It costs the day and a small offense, one weight lighter than if she found out.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: Telling her first is cheaper than being found out. A routine told once is told for the day.

short: While a rule of hers asks for permission, the commander asks her. She grants it, refuses, says not yet, or says to earn it. Her answer shows under the button.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The answer is the same for the same state. A refusal and a not yet relieve her own wanting a little. Doing it without asking is a slip against her rule.

short: She has not said how long. There is no timer, no deadline and no count on the card; only she knows when it ends, and it still ends.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A task, a hold or a punishment may run with no end named. The game keeps the end all the same: a task is still judged at its deadline and a hold still runs out. Ritual and drill women never leave one open.

short: She raises her hand. Press Space (or Brace) just before it lands. Too early, on a feint, or twice is a flinch; no press is none; one press in time is a brace.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: The time allowed is hers: it follows her manner and is shorter for the cruel ones. How good she is at it decides how often she feints. A brace pleases her and is respected; a flinch displeases her and some styles answer it. With the timing interaction off, or reduced motion, there is nothing to time: it lands.

short: Some women carry a heavy punishment out as a ceremony: steps in order by chip, in the commander's words, a number and postures. The last step carries it out.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: A woman of ritual, drill or regal bearing, or a vindictive one, does it for a punishment of weight three or more. A number she finds too low may be doubled by the harsher ones, and the commander is not told. A ceremony left open at the day's end is finished by her.

short: Put the device (a day), the key (up to seven days) or the calendar (up to three) in a holder's hands. It is signed; taking it back early counts as a refusal.
long: AUTHOR TO WRITE: With the device, every message to anyone else goes through her hand first. With the key she may be in the commander's quarters at any hour. With the calendar she fills the free slots of the days ahead, and those slots are lived as she set them. How she takes it depends on what it cost the commander and on how she is.
